source.text:
Ἐνετειλάμην σοι, φησίν, ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ ἐντολῇ ἵνα φυλάξῃς τὴν πίστιν καὶ τὸν φόβον καὶ τὴν ἐγκράτειαν. Ναί, φημί, κύριε. Ἀλλὰ νῦν θέλω σοι, φησί, δηλῶσαι καὶ τὰς δυνάμεις αὐτῶν, ἵνα νοήσῃς τίς αὐτῶν τίνα δύναμιν ἔχει καὶ ἐνέργειαν. διπλαῖ γάρ εἰσιν αἱ ἐνέργειαι αὐτῶν· κεῖνται οὖν ἐπὶ δικαίῳ καὶ ἀδίκῳ· 2. σὺ οὖν πίστευε τῷ δικαίῳ, τῷ δὲ ἀδίκῳ μὴ πιστεύσῃς· τὸ γὰρ δίκαιον ὀρθὴν ὁδὸν ἔχει, τὸ δὲ ἄδικον στρεβλήν. ἀλλὰ σὺ τῇ ὀρθῇ ὁδῷ πορεύου [καὶ ὁμαλῇ], τὴν δὲ στρεβλὴν ἔασον. 3. ἡ γὰρ στρεβλὴ ὁδὸς τρίβους οὐκ ἔχει, ἀλλ᾽ ἀνοδίας καὶ προσκόμματα πολλά, καὶ τραχεῖά ἐστι καὶ ἀκανθώδης. βλαβερὰ οὖν ἐστὶ τοῖς ἐν αὐτῇ πορευομένοις. 4. οἱ δὲ τῇ ὀρθῇ ὁδῷ πορευόμενοι ὁμαλῶς περιπατοῦσι καὶ ἀπροσκόπτως· οὔτε γὰρ τραχεῖά ἐστιν οὔτε ἀκανθώδης. βλέπεις οὖν ὅτι συμφορώτερόν ἐστι ταύτῃ τῇ ὁδῷ πορεύεσθαι. 5. Ἀρέσκει μοι, φημί, κύριε, ταύτῃ τῇ ὁδῷ πορεύεσθαι. Πορεύσῃ, φησί, καὶ ὃς ἂν ἐξ ὅλης καρδίας ἐπιστρέψῃ πρὸς Κύριον πορεύσεται ἐν αὐτῇ.

Ἄκουε νῦν, φησί, περὶ τῆς πίστεως. δύο εἰσὶν ἄγγελοι μετὰ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, εἷς τῆς δικαιοσύνης καὶ εἷς τῆς πονηρίας. 2. Πῶς οὖν, φημί, κύριε, γνώσομαι τὰς αὐτῶν ἐνεργείας, ὅτι ἀμφότεροι ἄγγελοι μετ᾽ ἐμοῦ κατοικοῦσιν; 3. Ἄκουε, φησί, καὶ σύνιε αὐτάς. ὁ μὲν τῆς δικαιοσύνης ἄγγελος τρυφερός ἐστι καὶ αἰσχυντηρὸς καὶ πρᾷος καὶ ἡσύχιος. ὅταν οὖν οὗτος ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν σου ἀναβῇ, εὐθέως λαλεῖ μετὰ σοῦ περὶ δικαιοσύνης, περὶ ἁγνείας, περὶ σεμνότητος, περὶ αὐταρκείας, περὶ παντὸς ἔργου δικαίου καὶ περὶ πάσης ἀρετῆς ἐνδόξου. ταῦτα πάντα ὅταν εἰς τὴν καρδίαν σου ἀναβῇ, γίνωσκε ὅτι ὁ ἄγγελος τῆς δικαιοσύνης μετὰ σοῦ ἐστί. [ταῦτα οὖν ἐστὶ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς δικαιοσύνης.] τούτῳ οὖν πίστευε καὶ τοῖς ἔργοις αὐτοῦ. 4. ὅρα νῦν καὶ τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς πονηρίας τὰ ἔργα. πρῶτον πάντων ὀξύχολός ἐστι καὶ πικρὸς καὶ ἄφρων, καὶ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ πονηρά, καταστρέφοντα τοὺς δούλους τοῦ Θεοῦ· ὅταν οὖν οὗτος ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν σου ἀναβῇ, γνῶθι αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ. 5. Πῶς, φημί, κύριε, νοήσω αὐτόν, οὐκ ἐπίσταμαι. Ἄκουε, φησίν. ὅταν ὀξυχολία σοί τις προσπέσῃ ἢ πικρία, γίνωσκε ὅτι αὐτός ἐστιν ἐν σοί· εἶτα ἐπιθυμία πράξεων πολλῶν καὶ πολυτέλεια ἐδεσμάτων πολλῶν καὶ μεθυσμάτων καὶ κραιπαλῶν πολλῶν καὶ ποικίλων τρυφῶν καὶ οὐ δεόντων, καὶ ἐπιθυμία γυναικῶν καὶ πλεονεξία καὶ ὑπερηφανία καὶ ἀλαζονεία, καὶ ὅσα τούτοις παραπλήσιά ἐστι καὶ ὅμοια. ταῦτα οὖν ὅταν ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν σου ἀναβῇ, γίνωσκε ὅτι ὁ ἄγγελος τῆς πονηρίας ἐστὶ μετὰ σοῦ. 6. σὺ οὖν ἐπιγνοὺς τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ ἀπόστα ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ καὶ μηδὲν αὐτῷ πίστευε, ὅτι τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ πονηρά εἰσι καὶ ἀσύμφορα τοῖς δούλοις τοῦ Θεοῦ. ἔχεις οὖν ἀμφοτέρων τῶν ἀγγέλων τὰς ἐνεργείας· σύνιε αὐτὰς καὶ πίστευε τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς δικαιοσύνης· 7. ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς πονηρίας ἀπόστηθι, ὅτι ἡ διδαχὴ αὐτοῦ πονηρά ἐστι παντὶ ἔργῳ· ἐὰν γὰρ ᾖ τις πιστὸς ἀνήρ, καὶ ἡ ἐνθύμησις τοῦ ἀγγέλου τούτου ἀναβῇ ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ, δεῖ τὸν ἄνδρα ἐκεῖνον ἢ τὴν γυναῖκα ἐξαμαρτῆσαί τι. 8. ἐὰν δὲ πάλιν πονηρότατός τις ᾖ ἀνὴρ ἢ γυνή, καὶ ἀναβῇ ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς δικαιοσύνης, ἐξ ἀνάγκης δεῖ αὐτὸν ἀγαθόν τι ποιῆσαι. 9. βλέπεις οὖν, φησίν, ὅτι καλόν ἐστι τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς δικαιοσύνης ἀκολουθεῖν, τῷ δὲ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς πονηρίας ἀποτάξασθαι. 10. τὰ μὲν περὶ τῆς πίστεως αὕτη ἡ ἐντολὴ δηλοῖ, ἵνα τοῖς ἔργοις τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς δικαιοσύνης πιστεύσῃς, καὶ ἐργασάμενος αὐτὰ ζήσῃ τῷ Θεῷ. πίστευε δὲ ὅτι τὰ ἔργα τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς πονηρίας χαλεπά ἐστι· μὴ ἐργαζόμενος οὖν αὐτὰ ζήσῃ τῷ Θεῷ.

translation.text:
I.1. “I commanded you in the first commandment,” he says, “to keep faith, fear and self-control.” “Yes, sir,” I say. “But now,” he says, “I also want to make known to you their powers, so that you may understand what power and activity each has. For their activities are twofold; they have to do with what is righteous and what is unrighteous.”[a]

I.2. “So trust what is righteous, but do not trust what is unrighteous. For what is righteous has a straight road, but what is unrighteous a crooked one. But you, walk on the straight [and level] road, and leave the crooked one.”[b]

I.3. “For the crooked road has no tracks, but pathless places and many stumbling blocks, and it is rough and thorny. So it is harmful to those who walk on it.”

I.4. “But those who travel the straight road walk smoothly and without stumbling, for it is neither rough nor thorny. You see, then, that it is more profitable to travel this road.”

I.5. “Sir,” I say, “I am pleased to travel this road.” “You will travel it,” he says, “and everyone who turns to the Lord with their whole heart will travel it.”[c]

II.1. “Now hear,” he says, “about faith. There are two angels with a person: one of righteousness and one of wickedness.”

II.2. “How, then, sir,” I say, “will I recognize their activities, since both angels dwell with me?”

II.3. “Listen,” he says, “and understand them. The angel of righteousness is tender, modest, gentle and quiet. When he rises up in your heart, he immediately speaks with you about righteousness, purity, dignity, contentment, every righteous deed and every glorious virtue. When all these things rise up in your heart, know that the angel of righteousness is with you. [These, then, are the works of the angel of righteousness.] So trust him and his works.”[d]

II.4. “Now look also at the works of the angel of wickedness. First of all, he is quick-tempered, bitter and senseless. His works are wicked, overthrowing God’s slaves. So when he rises up in your heart, recognize him by his works.”[e]

II.5. “Sir,” I say, “I do not know how I will recognize him.” “Listen,” he says. “When some quick temper or bitterness comes upon you, know that he is in you. Then come craving for many undertakings, extravagance in many foods and intoxicants and many revelries, luxuries of various kinds and things that are not fitting, desire for women, greed, haughtiness, boastfulness, and whatever is akin and similar to these. So when these things rise up in your heart, know that the angel of wickedness is with you.”[f]

II.6. “So when you recognize his works, withdraw from him and put no trust in him, because his works are wicked and unprofitable for God’s slaves. You have the activities of both angels. Discern them, and trust the angel of righteousness.”

II.7. “But withdraw from the angel of wickedness, because his teaching is wicked in every deed. For if someone is faithful and this angel’s thought rises up in their heart, that man or woman must commit some sin.”[g]

II.8. “But again, if a man or woman is very wicked and the works of the angel of righteousness rise up in their heart, they must of necessity do something good.”[g]

II.9. “You see, then,” he says, “that it is good to follow the angel of righteousness and to renounce the angel of wickedness.”

II.10. “As to faith, this commandment makes it clear that you should trust the works of the angel of righteousness and, by doing them, live to God. But believe that the works of the angel of wickedness are grievous. So by not doing them, you will live to God.”[h]

footnotes.text: The working Greek names faith, fear and self-control. Hilgenfeld1873 Vulgata printed47 prints abstinentiam for self-control as an emendation against reported poenitentiam, repentance; the printed Latin is not an intact manuscript vote for the emendation. Palatina printed91 has continentia. The right/wrong distinction retains the earlier contextual judgment that these refer to moral categories; it does not change them into classes of people.

The working edition brackets “and level”; its brackets remain in both English drafts. Lake1907 Plate VI line26 includes the phrase in the Athos diplomatic transcription. Bracketing in an edited text is not itself proof of a manuscript gap. The complete straight/crooked-road comparison is restored without transferring any text into the next reader slot.

The working Greek and Athos diplomatic transcription, Plate VI line29, explicitly say turns to the Lord with the whole heart. Palatina, Gebhardt/Harnack1877 printed93, likewise has wholehearted turning to God. Vulgata, Hilgenfeld1873 printed48, instead has wholehearted belief in the Lord. Alternative ending: “Everyone who believes in the Lord with their whole heart will travel it.” The explicit direction toward the Lord belongs to this source clause; it is not imposed as a uniform repentance formula elsewhere.

The working ii.3 has the righteous angel’s speech about righteousness, purity, dignity, contentment, every righteous deed and glorious virtue. Lake1907 Plate VI lines32–33 omits that intervening description and moves from the angel rising in the heart to recognizing his presence. Vulgata printed48 has a different expanded list: justice, modesty, chastity, kindness, forgiveness, love and piety. Palatina printed93 has justice, holiness, chastity, frugality, approved work and honorable virtue; its following works-of-the-wicked-messenger clause is marked corrupt by its editor and is not substituted into Greek. Retain the continuous working Greek with the shorter Athos alternative exposed. The working imperative “understand” is Gebhardt’s correction of reported A synieis, “you understand”; Lake prints that A form, while both printed Latin versions have intellige. The bracketed works sentence remains bracketed; contentment can also be rendered self-sufficiency, and modest can also mean reserved or bashful here.

Working ii.4 says “now,” a printed correction of reported Athos “therefore.” Lake1907 Plate VI line34 has oun, therefore. Alternative opening: “Therefore look also at the works of the angel of wickedness.” Latin Vulgata printed48 and Palatina printed93 use now. God’s slaves retains the prior recorded lexical/theological choice for douloi; servants is an alternative. Sir in dialogue is respectful address to the shepherd, distinguished from the Lord as God.

At ii.5 physical343 the print and Lake’s transcription read quick temper OR bitterness; the raw transcription’s nominative article hē was an error for the conjunction ē and is corrected to match the print. The complete Greek vice list is retained, including luxuries of various kinds AND things that are not fitting, preserving the earlier grammatical decision. The printed Vulgata list at49 differs and lacks several Greek items; Palatina printed95 is closer but not identical. Latin differences are not silently harmonized into the Greek.

The source states necessity in both directions: the faithful person under wicked influence must commit some sin, and the very wicked person under righteous influence must of necessity do something good. Both claims and the inclusion of man and woman are retained without softening must to may. The printed ii.8 subjunctive is Hilgenfeld’s correction of reported Athos optative eie; this is an edited grammatical form, not a new manuscript discovery.

Live to God preserves the Greek dative; live for God is an alternative. Both the positive doing-righteous-works clause and the negative not-doing-wicked-works clause are retained. The printed Vulgata at50 ends this mandate with a different positive following/believing summary, while Palatina printed95 retains the negative abstaining clause. No versional ending is inserted as if it were identical Greek. Sinaiticus ends within Mandate4iii and cannot decide Mandate6 readings.

lexical_decisions.rationale: Default rendering per project policy; here it names a virtue to be guarded alongside fear and self-control.
Moral-exhortation context; concise and weighty. The object is implicitly God.
Standard moral virtue; contemporary and clear without archaic tone.
Refers to the effective capacity of the virtues; preserves concrete sense.
Describes what they effect/do; 'activities' is natural English and avoids metaphysical overtones of 'energies'.
Moral-spiritual frame throughout the unit; 'righteous' pairs with 'angel of righteousness' later.
Maintains symmetry with 'righteous' and moral nuance, not merely legal injustice.
Concrete road imagery; 'crooked' captures στρεβλή's moral-twisted connotation.
Footpath nuance fits the road metaphor; 'tracks' contrasts with 'trackless' below.
Conveys absence of usable roads; keeps the metaphor vivid.
Common moral metaphor; concrete and idiomatic.
Plain English for uneven, harsh terrain.
Natural, vivid description; keeps the concrete image.
Standard ethical term; suits inner sourness linked to wicked influence.
Here of appetitive urge; 'craving' fits vices list tone.
Here the context is restless busyness; 'undertakings' implies many pursuits.
Conveys excess rather than mere quality; matches vice catalog.
'Foods' is clear and broad; 'dishes/viands' is archaic.
Specifies alcoholic drinks with intoxicating effect; succinct and precise.
'Revelries' captures feasting/riotous excess without archaic or moralistic inflation.
In a vice list, 'luxuries' concisely names soft-living indulgence.
Plain English; moral impropriety without formality.
Modern equivalent; 'covetousness' is accurate but archaic in tone.
Highlights disdainful superiority, distinct from ἀλαζονεία.
Self-exalting display; 'boastfulness' pairs well with 'haughtiness'.
Inner consideration/impulse arising in the heart; 'thought' keeps idiomatic clarity.
Transparently expresses moral failure; indefinite 'some' reflects τι.
Idiomatic for decisive parting; moral break with the wicked angel.
Neutral term; context supplies moral evaluation.
Common early-Christian idiom for spiritually unhelpful; fits contrast with 'live to God'.
Per project policy, 'slaves' when bonded belonging is salient; here opposed to another lord’s works.
Carries the sense of hard/cruel; 'grievous' suits moral weight.
Moral discernment is in view; 'discern' fits evaluative context.
Imperative of spatial/moral separation; 'withdraw' is vivid and brief.
With personal object and even with 'works', 'trust' best conveys allegiance/credence in moral instruction.
Standard moral metaphor of discipleship/path.
Preserves dative idiom familiar in early Christian diction; noted in theological decisions.
Direction is explicit in restored i5; distinguish Vulgata belief from Greek/Palatina turning.
Respectful address to the shepherd; retain divine Lord elsewhere.
Retain complete moral description from working Greek with variant list disclosed.
Printed conjecture supported by Latin imperatives remains explicitly distinguished from A.
Do not present a printed correction as unanimous manuscript wording.

theological_decisions.issue: Genitive titles for angels (τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς δικαιοσύνης / τῆς πονηρίας)
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Render as 'angel of righteousness' / 'angel of wickedness'
theological_decisions.rationale: The genitive denotes the moral quality these angels represent or administer; preserving it keeps Hermas’s moral taxonomy explicit.
Per project policy, 'slave' highlights belonging and allegiance; here contrasted with trusting the wicked angel’s works.
theological_decisions.doctrine_reference: Translation philosophy: contested terms — doulos → slave where bonded nature salient.

theological_decisions.rationale: The dative expresses orientation; 'to God' preserves early Christian idiom and rhetorical symmetry within the mandate.

theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Render 'trust' rather than 'believe' when the object is a person or 'works'
theological_decisions.rationale: 'Trust' fits allegiance/credence; 'believe the works' is awkward in English while 'trust' is idiomatic and maintains the exhortational force.

theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Render 'faithful person' (inclusive of man or woman by following clause)
theological_decisions.rationale: Hermas immediately includes 'that man or that woman'; 'faithful person' captures moral-religious status without gender restriction.

theological_decisions.issue: Internal moral influence phrased as 'he is in you'
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Translate literally to preserve Hermas’s moral-psychological imagery
alternative_readings: he is at work in you
theological_decisions.rationale: Hermas depicts the presence of either angel in the heart via arising thoughts; retaining 'in you' keeps the vivid interior imagery.

theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Retain whole-heart turning, the two angels, complete virtues and vices, both necessity claims and positive/negative work clauses.
theological_decisions.rationale: Do not replace difficult source claims with a different doctrine or collapse versional differences into Greek.

revisions.from: and pleasures of various kinds that are not fitting
revisions.to: and luxuries of various kinds, and things that are not fitting
revisions.rationale: The Greek 'καὶ ποικίλων τρυφῶν καὶ οὐ δεόντων' contains two distinct genitive items. 'δεόντων' is neuter plural ('things not fitting') and stands as its own substantive in the list, rather than modifying the feminine 'τρυφῶν'. Additionally, the project's lexical decision for τρυφῶν is 'luxuries', not 'pleasures'. | Adjudicator: The reviewer is grammatically correct. In the Greek phrase 'καὶ ποικίλων τρυφῶν καὶ οὐ δεόντων', 'τρυφῶν' is a feminine noun (genitive plural) while 'δεόντων' is a neuter participle (genitive plural).

So you—trust what is righteous, but do not trust what is unrighteous; for what is righteous has a straight road, but what is unrighteous a crooked one. But you, walk on the straight [and level][1] road, and leave the crooked.

For the crooked road has no tracks, but trackless places and many stumbling blocks; and it is rough and thorny. Therefore it is harmful; if bitterness should come upon you, know that he is in you. Then come the craving for many undertakings, and extravagance in many foods, and intoxicants and many revelries, and luxuries of various kinds, and things that are not fitting; and desire for women, and greed, and haughtiness, and boastfulness, and whatever things are akin and similar to these. Therefore, whenever these things rise up upon your heart, know that the angel of wickedness is with you.

So when you recognize his works, withdraw from him and put no trust in him, because his works are wicked and unprofitable for God’s slaves. You therefore have the activities of both angels; discern them, and trust the angel of righteousness. But withdraw from the angel of wickedness, because his teaching is wicked in every deed. For if someone is a faithful person, and the thought of this angel rises up upon that one’s heart, that man or that woman is bound to commit some sin. But if again someone is a very wicked person, man or woman, and the works of the angel of righteousness rise up upon that one’s heart, that person of necessity must do something good. You see then,” he says, “that it is good to follow the angel of righteousness, and to renounce the angel of wickedness. As to faith, this commandment makes it clear: that you should trust the works of the angel of righteousness, and, having done them, live to God.[3] But believe that the works of the angel of wickedness are grievous; so by not doing them, you will live to God.”

For their activities are twofold; so they are set over the righteous and the unrighteous. So you—trust the righteous, but do not trust the unrighteous; for righteousness has a straight path, but unrighteousness a crooked one. But you, walk on the straight [and level][1] path, and leave the crooked.

Therefore, whenever these things rise up in your heart, know that the angel of wickedness is with you.

So when you recognize his works, withdraw from him and put no trust in him, because his works are wicked and harmful to God’s slaves. You therefore have the activities of both angels; understand them, and trust the angel of righteousness. But withdraw from the angel of wickedness, because his teaching is wicked in every deed. For if someone is a faithful man, and the thought of this angel rises up in his heart, that man or woman must commit some sin. But if again some man or woman is very wicked, and the works of the angel of righteousness rise up in his or her heart, that person must of necessity do something good. You see then,” he says, “that it is good to follow the angel of righteousness, and to renounce the angel of wickedness. As to faith, this commandment makes it clear: that you should trust the works of the angel of righteousness, and, having done them, live to God.[3] But believe that the works of the angel of wickedness are grievous; so by not doing them, you will live to God.”
revisions.rationale: Improved lexical accuracy and completeness: rendered κεῖνται as “are set over,” δικαίῳ/ἀδίκῳ as “the righteous/the unrighteous,” and ὁδός as “path” consistently in the road metaphor. Restored omitted material after “Therefore it is harmful” (“But hear also the works of the other way. First of all... quick temper”), and adjusted several vice terms for closer sense (e.g., “drinks,” “drunken sprees,” “arrogance”). Smoothed English while keeping a formal register.

He says, “I commanded you in the first commandment to keep faith and fear and self-control.”[2] “Yes, lord,” I say. “But now,” he says, “I want also to make known to you their powers, so that you may understand what power and what activity each of them has. For their activities are twofold; so they have to do with what is righteous and what is unrighteous. So you—trust what is righteous, but do not trust what is unrighteous; for what is righteous has a straight road, but what is unrighteous a crooked one. But you, walk on the straight [and level][1] road, and leave the crooked.

For the crooked road has no tracks, but trackless places and many stumbling blocks; and it is rough and thorny. Therefore it is harmful; if bitterness should come upon you, know that he is in you. Then come the craving for many undertakings, and extravagance in many foods, and intoxicants and many revelries, and luxuries of various kinds, and things that are not fitting; and desire for women, and greed, and haughtiness, and boastfulness, and whatever things are akin and similar to these. Therefore, whenever these things rise up upon your heart, know that the angel of wickedness is with you.

So when you recognize his works, withdraw from him and put no trust in him, because his works are wicked and unprofitable for God’s slaves. You therefore have the activities of both angels; discern them, and trust the angel of righteousness. But withdraw from the angel of wickedness, because his teaching is wicked in every deed. For if someone is a faithful person, and the thought of this angel rises up upon that one’s heart, that man or that woman is bound to commit some sin. But if again someone is a very wicked person, man or woman, and the works of the angel of righteousness rise up upon that one’s heart, that person of necessity must do something good. You see then,” he says, “that it is good to follow the angel of righteousness, and to renounce the angel of wickedness. As to faith, this commandment makes it clear: that you should trust the works of the angel of righteousness, and, having done them, live to God.[3] But believe that the works of the angel of wickedness are grievous; so by not doing them, you will live to God.”

Ἐνετειλάμην σοι, φησίν, ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ ἐντολῇ ἵνα φυλάξῃς τὴν πίστιν καὶ τὸν φόβον καὶ τὴν ἐγκράτειαν. Ναί, φημί, κύριε. Ἀλλὰ νῦν θέλω σοι, φησί, δηλῶσαι καὶ τὰς δυνάμεις αὐτῶν, ἵνα νοήσῃς τίς αὐτῶν τίνα δύναμιν ἔχει καὶ ἐνέργειαν. διπλαῖ γάρ εἰσιν αἱ ἐνέργειαι αὐτῶν· κεῖνται οὖν ἐπὶ δικαίῳ καὶ ἀδίκῳ· 2. σὺ οὖν πίστευε τῷ δικαίῳ, τῷ δὲ ἀδίκῳ μὴ πιστεύσῃς· τὸ γὰρ δίκαιον ὀρθὴν ὁδὸν ἔχει, τὸ δὲ ἄδικον στρεβλήν. ἀλλὰ σὺ τῇ ὀρθῇ ὁδῷ πορεύου [καὶ ὁμαλῇ], τὴν δὲ στρεβλὴν ἔασον. 3. ἡ γὰρ στρεβλὴ ὁδὸς τρίβους οὐκ ἔχει, ἀλλ᾽ ἀνοδίας καὶ προσκόμματα πολλά, καὶ τραχεῖά ἐστι καὶ ἀκανθώδης. βλαβερὰ οὖν ἐστὶ τοῖς ἐν αὐτῇ πορευομένοις. 4. οἱ δὲ τῇ ὀρθῇ ὁδῷ πορευόμενοι ὁμαλῶς περιπατοῦσι καὶ ἀπροσκόπτως· οὔτε γὰρ τραχεῖά ἐστιν οὔτε ἀκανθώδης. βλέπεις οὖν ὅτι συμφορώτερόν ἐστι ταύτῃ τῇ ὁδῷ πορεύεσθαι. 5. Ἀρέσκει μοι, φημί, κύριε, ταύτῃ τῇ ὁδῷ πορεύεσθαι. Πορεύσῃ, φησί, καὶ ὃς ἂν ἐξ ὅλης καρδίας ἐπιστρέψῃ πρὸς Κύριον πορεύσεται ἐν αὐτῇ.

Ἄκουε νῦν, φησί, περὶ τῆς πίστεως. δύο εἰσὶν ἄγγελοι μετὰ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, εἷς τῆς δικαιοσύνης καὶ εἷς τῆς πονηρίας. 2. Πῶς οὖν, φημί, κύριε, γνώσομαι τὰς αὐτῶν ἐνεργείας, ὅτι ἀμφότεροι ἄγγελοι μετ᾽ ἐμοῦ κατοικοῦσιν; 3. Ἄκουε, φησί, καὶ σύνιε αὐτάς. ὁ μὲν τῆς δικαιοσύνης ἄγγελος τρυφερός ἐστι καὶ αἰσχυντηρὸς καὶ πρᾷος καὶ ἡσύχιος. ὅταν οὖν οὗτος ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν σου ἀναβῇ, εὐθέως λαλεῖ μετὰ σοῦ περὶ δικαιοσύνης, περὶ ἁγνείας, περὶ σεμνότητος, περὶ αὐταρκείας, περὶ παντὸς ἔργου δικαίου καὶ περὶ πάσης ἀρετῆς ἐνδόξου. ταῦτα πάντα ὅταν εἰς τὴν καρδίαν σου ἀναβῇ, γίνωσκε ὅτι ὁ ἄγγελος τῆς δικαιοσύνης μετὰ σοῦ ἐστί. [ταῦτα οὖν ἐστὶ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς δικαιοσύνης.] τούτῳ οὖν πίστευε καὶ τοῖς ἔργοις αὐτοῦ. 4. ὅρα νῦν καὶ τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς πονηρίας τὰ ἔργα. πρῶτον πάντων ὀξύχολός ἐστι καὶ πικρὸς καὶ ἄφρων, καὶ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ πονηρά, καταστρέφοντα τοὺς δούλους τοῦ Θεοῦ· ὅταν οὖν οὗτος ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν σου ἀναβῇ, γνῶθι αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ. 5. Πῶς, φημί, κύριε, νοήσω αὐτόν, οὐκ ἐπίσταμαι. Ἄκουε, φησίν. ὅταν ὀξυχολία σοί τις προσπέσῃ ἢ πικρία, γίνωσκε ὅτι αὐτός ἐστιν ἐν σοί· εἶτα ἐπιθυμία πράξεων πολλῶν καὶ πολυτέλεια ἐδεσμάτων πολλῶν καὶ μεθυσμάτων καὶ κραιπαλῶν πολλῶν καὶ ποικίλων τρυφῶν καὶ οὐ δεόντων, καὶ ἐπιθυμία γυναικῶν καὶ πλεονεξία καὶ ὑπερηφανία καὶ ἀλαζονεία, καὶ ὅσα τούτοις παραπλήσιά ἐστι καὶ ὅμοια. ταῦτα οὖν ὅταν ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν σου ἀναβῇ, γίνωσκε ὅτι ὁ ἄγγελος τῆς πονηρίας ἐστὶ μετὰ σοῦ. 6. σὺ οὖν ἐπιγνοὺς τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ ἀπόστα ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ καὶ μηδὲν αὐτῷ πίστευε, ὅτι τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ πονηρά εἰσι καὶ ἀσύμφορα τοῖς δούλοις τοῦ Θεοῦ. ἔχεις οὖν ἀμφοτέρων τῶν ἀγγέλων τὰς ἐνεργείας· σύνιε αὐτὰς καὶ πίστευε τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς δικαιοσύνης· 7. ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς πονηρίας ἀπόστηθι, ὅτι ἡ διδαχὴ αὐτοῦ πονηρά ἐστι παντὶ ἔργῳ· ἐὰν γὰρ ᾖ τις πιστὸς ἀνήρ, καὶ ἡ ἐνθύμησις τοῦ ἀγγέλου τούτου ἀναβῇ ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ, δεῖ τὸν ἄνδρα ἐκεῖνον ἢ τὴν γυναῖκα ἐξαμαρτῆσαί τι. 8. ἐὰν δὲ πάλιν πονηρότατός τις ᾖ ἀνὴρ ἢ γυνή, καὶ ἀναβῇ ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς δικαιοσύνης, ἐξ ἀνάγκης δεῖ αὐτὸν ἀγαθόν τι ποιῆσαι. 9. βλέπεις οὖν, φησίν, ὅτι καλόν ἐστι τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς δικαιοσύνης ἀκολουθεῖν, τῷ δὲ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς πονηρίας ἀποτάξασθαι. 10. τὰ μὲν περὶ τῆς πίστεως αὕτη ἡ ἐντολὴ δηλοῖ, ἵνα τοῖς ἔργοις τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς δικαιοσύνης πιστεύσῃς, καὶ ἐργασάμενος αὐτὰ ζήσῃ τῷ Θεῷ. πίστευε δὲ ὅτι τὰ ἔργα τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς πονηρίας χαλεπά ἐστι· μὴ ἐργαζόμενος οὖν αὐτὰ ζήσῃ τῷ Θεῷ.

translation.text:
I.1. He says, “In the first commandment I told you to keep faith, fear and self-control.” “Yes, sir,” I say. “Now I also want to explain their powers,” he says. “Then you can understand the power of each and how each works. Their activities are twofold. They have to do with what is right and what is wrong.”[a]

I.2. “Trust what is right. Do not trust what is wrong. What is right has a straight road. What is wrong has a crooked one. Walk on the straight [and level] road. Leave the crooked one.”[b]

I.3. “The crooked road has no tracks. It has places with no path and many stumbling blocks. It is rough and thorny, so it harms the people who walk on it.”

I.4. “People on the straight road walk smoothly, without stumbling. It is neither rough nor thorny. You see that it is better to travel this road.”

I.5. I say, “Sir, I am pleased to travel this road.” He says, “You will travel it. So will everyone who turns to the Lord with their whole heart.”[c]

II.1. He says, “Now hear about faith. Two angels are with a person: an angel of righteousness and an angel of wickedness.”

II.2. I say, “Sir, how can I recognize what each does, since both angels live with me?”

II.3. “Listen and understand them,” he says. “The angel of righteousness is tender, modest, gentle and quiet. When he rises up in your heart, he speaks with you at once about righteousness, purity, dignity, contentment, every right deed and every glorious virtue. When these things rise up in your heart, know that the angel of righteousness is with you. [These are the works of the angel of righteousness.] Trust him and his works.”[d]

II.4. “Now look at what the angel of wickedness does. He is quick-tempered, bitter and senseless. His works are evil and overthrow God’s slaves. When he rises up in your heart, recognize him by what he does.”[e]

II.5. I say, “Sir, I do not know how to recognize him.” “Listen,” he says. “When quick temper or bitterness comes over you, know that he is in you. Then come cravings for many undertakings, costly foods and intoxicating drinks, many revelries, all kinds of luxuries and things that are not fitting. There are also desire for women, greed, haughtiness, boastfulness and other things like these. When these things rise up in your heart, know that the angel of wickedness is with you.”[f]

II.6. “When you recognize his works, leave him and put no trust in him. His works are evil and do no good for God’s slaves. You know what both angels do. Discern their activities and trust the angel of righteousness.”

II.7. “Leave the angel of wickedness. His teaching is evil in every deed. If someone is faithful and this angel’s thought rises up in their heart, that man or woman must commit some sin.”[g]

II.8. “Again, a man or woman may be very wicked. If the works of the angel of righteousness rise up in their heart, they must necessarily do something good.”[g]

II.9. He says, “You see that it is good to follow the angel of righteousness and renounce the angel of wickedness.”

II.10. “This commandment explains faith. Trust the works of the angel of righteousness. By doing them, you will live to God. Believe that the works of the angel of wickedness are grievous. By not doing them, you will live to God.”[h]

footnotes.text: The working Greek names faith, fear and self-control. Hilgenfeld1873 Vulgata printed47 prints abstinentiam for self-control as an emendation against reported poenitentiam, repentance; the printed Latin is not an intact manuscript vote for the emendation. Palatina printed91 has continentia. The right/wrong distinction retains the earlier contextual judgment that these refer to moral categories; it does not change them into classes of people.

The working edition brackets “and level”; its brackets remain in both English drafts. Lake1907 Plate VI line26 includes the phrase in the Athos diplomatic transcription. Bracketing in an edited text is not itself proof of a manuscript gap. The complete straight/crooked-road comparison is restored without transferring any text into the next reader slot.

The working Greek and Athos diplomatic transcription, Plate VI line29, explicitly say turns to the Lord with the whole heart. Palatina, Gebhardt/Harnack1877 printed93, likewise has wholehearted turning to God. Vulgata, Hilgenfeld1873 printed48, instead has wholehearted belief in the Lord. Alternative ending: “Everyone who believes in the Lord with their whole heart will travel it.” The explicit direction toward the Lord belongs to this source clause; it is not imposed as a uniform repentance formula elsewhere.

The working ii.3 has the righteous angel’s speech about righteousness, purity, dignity, contentment, every righteous deed and glorious virtue. Lake1907 Plate VI lines32–33 omits that intervening description and moves from the angel rising in the heart to recognizing his presence. Vulgata printed48 has a different expanded list: justice, modesty, chastity, kindness, forgiveness, love and piety. Palatina printed93 has justice, holiness, chastity, frugality, approved work and honorable virtue; its following works-of-the-wicked-messenger clause is marked corrupt by its editor and is not substituted into Greek. Retain the continuous working Greek with the shorter Athos alternative exposed. The working imperative “understand” is Gebhardt’s correction of reported A synieis, “you understand”; Lake prints that A form, while both printed Latin versions have intellige. The bracketed works sentence remains bracketed; contentment can also be rendered self-sufficiency, and modest can also mean reserved or bashful here.

Working ii.4 says “now,” a printed correction of reported Athos “therefore.” Lake1907 Plate VI line34 has oun, therefore. Alternative opening: “Therefore look also at the works of the angel of wickedness.” Latin Vulgata printed48 and Palatina printed93 use now. God’s slaves retains the prior recorded lexical/theological choice for douloi; servants is an alternative. Sir in dialogue is respectful address to the shepherd, distinguished from the Lord as God.

At ii.5 physical343 the print and Lake’s transcription read quick temper OR bitterness; the raw transcription’s nominative article hē was an error for the conjunction ē and is corrected to match the print. The complete Greek vice list is retained, including luxuries of various kinds AND things that are not fitting, preserving the earlier grammatical decision. The printed Vulgata list at49 differs and lacks several Greek items; Palatina printed95 is closer but not identical. Latin differences are not silently harmonized into the Greek.

The source states necessity in both directions: the faithful person under wicked influence must commit some sin, and the very wicked person under righteous influence must of necessity do something good. Both claims and the inclusion of man and woman are retained without softening must to may. The printed ii.8 subjunctive is Hilgenfeld’s correction of reported Athos optative eie; this is an edited grammatical form, not a new manuscript discovery.

Live to God preserves the Greek dative; live for God is an alternative. Both the positive doing-righteous-works clause and the negative not-doing-wicked-works clause are retained. The printed Vulgata at50 ends this mandate with a different positive following/believing summary, while Palatina printed95 retains the negative abstaining clause. No versional ending is inserted as if it were identical Greek. Sinaiticus ends within Mandate4iii and cannot decide Mandate6 readings.

lexical_decisions.rationale: Default rendering per project policy; here it names a virtue to be guarded alongside fear and self-control.
Moral-exhortation context; concise and weighty. The object is implicitly God.
Standard moral virtue; contemporary and clear without archaic tone.
Refers to the effective capacity of the virtues; preserves concrete sense.
Describes what they effect/do; 'activities' is natural English and avoids metaphysical overtones of 'energies'.
Moral-spiritual frame throughout the unit; 'righteous' pairs with 'angel of righteousness' later.
Maintains symmetry with 'righteous' and moral nuance, not merely legal injustice.
Concrete road imagery; 'crooked' captures στρεβλή's moral-twisted connotation.
Footpath nuance fits the road metaphor; 'tracks' contrasts with 'trackless' below.
Conveys absence of usable roads; keeps the metaphor vivid.
Common moral metaphor; concrete and idiomatic.
Plain English for uneven, harsh terrain.
Natural, vivid description; keeps the concrete image.
Standard ethical term; suits inner sourness linked to wicked influence.
Here of appetitive urge; 'craving' fits vices list tone.
Here the context is restless busyness; 'undertakings' implies many pursuits.
Conveys excess rather than mere quality; matches vice catalog.
'Foods' is clear and broad; 'dishes/viands' is archaic.
Specifies alcoholic drinks with intoxicating effect; succinct and precise.
'Revelries' captures feasting/riotous excess without archaic or moralistic inflation.
In a vice list, 'luxuries' concisely names soft-living indulgence.
Plain English; moral impropriety without formality.
Modern equivalent; 'covetousness' is accurate but archaic in tone.
Highlights disdainful superiority, distinct from ἀλαζονεία.
Self-exalting display; 'boastfulness' pairs well with 'haughtiness'.
Inner consideration/impulse arising in the heart; 'thought' keeps idiomatic clarity.
Transparently expresses moral failure; indefinite 'some' reflects τι.
Idiomatic for decisive parting; moral break with the wicked angel.
Neutral term; context supplies moral evaluation.
Common early-Christian idiom for spiritually unhelpful; fits contrast with 'live to God'.
Per project policy, 'slaves' when bonded belonging is salient; here opposed to another lord’s works.
Carries the sense of hard/cruel; 'grievous' suits moral weight.
Moral discernment is in view; 'discern' fits evaluative context.
Imperative of spatial/moral separation; 'withdraw' is vivid and brief.
With personal object and even with 'works', 'trust' best conveys allegiance/credence in moral instruction.
Standard moral metaphor of discipleship/path.
Preserves dative idiom familiar in early Christian diction; noted in theological decisions.
Direction is explicit in restored i5; distinguish Vulgata belief from Greek/Palatina turning.
Respectful address to the shepherd; retain divine Lord elsewhere.
Retain complete moral description from working Greek with variant list disclosed.
Printed conjecture supported by Latin imperatives remains explicitly distinguished from A.
Do not present a printed correction as unanimous manuscript wording.

theological_decisions.issue: Genitive titles for angels (τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῆς δικαιοσύνης / τῆς πονηρίας)
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Render as 'angel of righteousness' / 'angel of wickedness'
theological_decisions.rationale: The genitive denotes the moral quality these angels represent or administer; preserving it keeps Hermas’s moral taxonomy explicit.
Per project policy, 'slave' highlights belonging and allegiance; here contrasted with trusting the wicked angel’s works.
theological_decisions.doctrine_reference: Translation philosophy: contested terms — doulos → slave where bonded nature salient.

theological_decisions.rationale: The dative expresses orientation; 'to God' preserves early Christian idiom and rhetorical symmetry within the mandate.

theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Render 'trust' rather than 'believe' when the object is a person or 'works'
theological_decisions.rationale: 'Trust' fits allegiance/credence; 'believe the works' is awkward in English while 'trust' is idiomatic and maintains the exhortational force.

theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Render 'faithful person' (inclusive of man or woman by following clause)
theological_decisions.rationale: Hermas immediately includes 'that man or that woman'; 'faithful person' captures moral-religious status without gender restriction.

theological_decisions.issue: Internal moral influence phrased as 'he is in you'
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Translate literally to preserve Hermas’s moral-psychological imagery
alternative_readings: he is at work in you
theological_decisions.rationale: Hermas depicts the presence of either angel in the heart via arising thoughts; retaining 'in you' keeps the vivid interior imagery.

theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Retain whole-heart turning, the two angels, complete virtues and vices, both necessity claims and positive/negative work clauses.
theological_decisions.rationale: Do not replace difficult source claims with a different doctrine or collapse versional differences into Greek.

II.2. “How, then, sir,” I say, “will I recognize their activities, since both angels dwell with me?”

II.3. “Listen,” he says, “and understand them. The angel of righteousness is tender, modest, gentle and quiet. When he rises up in your heart, he immediately speaks with you about righteousness, purity, dignity, contentment, every righteous deed and every glorious virtue. When all these things rise up in your heart, know that the angel of righteousness is with you. [These, then, are the works of the angel of righteousness.] So trust him and his works.”[d]

II.4. “Now look also at the works of the angel of wickedness. First of all, he is quick-tempered, bitter and senseless. His works are wicked, overthrowing God’s servants. So when he rises up in your heart, recognize him by his works.”[e]

II.5. “Sir,” I say, “I do not know how I will recognize him.” “Listen,” he says. “When some quick temper or bitterness comes upon you, know that he is in you. Then come craving for many undertakings, extravagance in many foods and intoxicants and many revelries, luxuries of various kinds and things that are not fitting, desire for women, greed, haughtiness, boastfulness, and whatever is akin and similar to these. So when these things rise up in your heart, know that the angel of wickedness is with you.”[f]

II.6. “So when you recognize his works, withdraw from him and put no trust in him, because his works are wicked and unprofitable for God’s servants. You have the activities of both angels. Discern them, and trust the angel of righteousness.”

II.7. “But withdraw from the angel of wickedness, because his teaching is wicked in every deed. For if someone is faithful and this angel’s thought rises up in their heart, that man or woman must commit some sin.”[g]

II.8. “But again, if a man or woman is very wicked and the works of the angel of righteousness rise up in their heart, they must of necessity do something good.”[g]

II.9. “You see, then,” he says, “that it is good to follow the angel of righteousness and to renounce the angel of wickedness.”

II.10. “As to faith, this commandment makes it clear that you should trust the works of the angel of righteousness and, by doing them, live to God. But believe that the works of the angel of wickedness are grievous. So by not doing them, you will live to God.”[h]

I.1. He says, “In the first commandment I told you to keep faith, fear and self-control.” “Yes, sir,” I say. “Now I also want to explain their powers,” he says. “Then you can understand the power of each and how each works. Their activities are twofold. They have to do with what is right and what is wrong.”[a]

I.2. “Trust what is right. Do not trust what is wrong. What is right has a straight road. What is wrong has a crooked one. Walk on the straight [and level] road. Leave the crooked one.”[b]

I.3. “The crooked road has no tracks. It has places with no path and many stumbling blocks. It is rough and thorny, so it harms the people who walk on it.”

I.4. “People on the straight road walk smoothly, without stumbling. It is neither rough nor thorny. You see that it is better to travel this road.”

I.5. I say, “Sir, I am pleased to travel this road.” He says, “You will travel it. So will everyone who turns to the Lord with their whole heart.”[c]

II.1. He says, “Now hear about faith. Two angels are with a person: an angel of righteousness and an angel of wickedness.”

II.2. I say, “Sir, how can I recognize what each does, since both angels live with me?”

II.3. “Listen and understand them,” he says. “The angel of righteousness is tender, modest, gentle and quiet. When he rises up in your heart, he speaks with you at once about righteousness, purity, dignity, contentment, every right deed and every glorious virtue. When these things rise up in your heart, know that the angel of righteousness is with you. [These are the works of the angel of righteousness.] Trust him and his works.”[d]

II.4. “Now look at what the angel of wickedness does. He is quick-tempered, bitter and senseless. His works are evil and overthrow God’s servants. When he rises up in your heart, recognize him by what he does.”[e]

II.5. I say, “Sir, I do not know how to recognize him.” “Listen,” he says. “When quick temper or bitterness comes over you, know that he is in you. Then come cravings for many undertakings, costly foods and intoxicating drinks, many revelries, all kinds of luxuries and things that are not fitting. There are also desire for women, greed, haughtiness, boastfulness and other things like these. When these things rise up in your heart, know that the angel of wickedness is with you.”[f]

II.6. “When you recognize his works, leave him and put no trust in him. His works are evil and do no good for God’s servants. You know what both angels do. Discern their activities and trust the angel of righteousness.”

II.7. “Leave the angel of wickedness. His teaching is evil in every deed. If someone is faithful and this angel’s thought rises up in their heart, that man or woman must commit some sin.”[g]

II.8. “Again, a man or woman may be very wicked. If the works of the angel of righteousness rise up in their heart, they must necessarily do something good.”[g]

II.9. He says, “You see that it is good to follow the angel of righteousness and renounce the angel of wickedness.”

II.10. “This commandment explains faith. Trust the works of the angel of righteousness. By doing them, you will live to God. Believe that the works of the angel of wickedness are grievous. By not doing them, you will live to God.”[h]
